title: Good and Evil
html:
‘Mandala’s Guardian’ was a mysterious constellation.

Unlike other constellations, this one rarely appeared in channels and seldom sent messages even when present.

At regular intervals, the constellation selected an ‘incarnation’ and granted that incarnation the attribute of ‘Reincarnator’.

Nirvana, standing before me, was one of the reincarnators born that way.

「(You have no idea how terrible reincarnation is. There must be no more reincarnators.)」

“That's not for you to decide.”

Nirvana and I looked at Yoo Sangah at the same time.

Still unable to grasp the situation, she blinked blankly. She was probably working hard to understand the context of our conversation.

「(······Doesn't that woman already have a sponsor?)」

“Not anymore. When I fought in <Gigantomachia>, I asked Dionysus to sever the connection, and he did.”

「(‘Olympus’ agreed so readily? How did you cover that enormous probability cost?)」

I merely shrugged.

I didn't have time to explain the details of the battle against <Olympus> or my deal with Dionysus anyway.

“Read it through the ‘wall’ later. You're reading everything I do anyway, aren't you? More importantly, hurry up and answer my question. Where's your sponsor now?”

「(My connection with him was also severed when I was absorbed by the ‘wall’. I don't know where he is now. But······.)」

Nirvana gave me a sidelong look and continued.

「(I suspect you've already guessed.)」

That was true.

The only reason I'd asked Nirvana was to turn my guess into certainty.

“Yoo Sangah-ssi, don't worry too much. They're not as bad as they look―”

I didn't get to finish.

Rrrrrrumble!

With the sensation of the entire space contracting, my body was being expelled from the Library. Startled, Yoo Sangah reached toward me, but I was already scattering amid the sparks.

「In so lent Kim Dok ja.」

And those were the last words I heard.

*

「“······Has Dokja-ssi still not woken up?”」

「“No.”」

「“It's already the third day······.”」

As voices rippled toward me from far away, I slowly regained consciousness.

Uncomfortable sensations I couldn't quite describe washed over me all at once.

How could I put it? Like being tortured with electricity.

「“He's not an electric eel······What on earth is going on······?”」

「“What happened to Sangah-unnie? Even her entire incarnation body suddenly disappeared······.”」

Hearing those faint voices, I slowly began to piece together the situation I was in.

······Damn it. Had I really been unconscious for three days?

I'd regained consciousness, but I couldn't move at all.

Tzzzzzzzt!

[Your actions to prevent a companion's death have been detected by the ‘Probability Suitability Review’.]

[You are currently suffering the aftereffects of a ‘probability storm’.]

[Nearly all your actions will be restricted for a total of 5 days.]

[Remaining restriction period: 2 days 3 hours 31 minutes]

Despite all my efforts to avoid it, it seemed I'd ended up caught in a probability storm after all. Under the circumstances, it was a miracle I'd gotten off this lightly.

[You have received messages through ‘Dokkaebi Communication’.]

They were from Bihyung.

―Kim Dokja, you lunatic.

―Do you want ‘The Indescribable Distance’ to eat you again?

―If I hadn't put the brakes on beforehand, a catastrophe would've hit Earth. You keep getting lucky and getting away with it, so you think probability doesn't mean shit?

Bihyung's messages continued for quite a while.

If I wanted to reach the scenarios' ending safely, I had to build up probability properly. I shouldn't make <Star Stream> hate me. The usual nagging. Since when had he become such a scold?

―Anyway, I'll let it slide this time. Be careful next time. The will of <Star Stream> is watching you very closely because of this.

I hadn't known that forcibly tearing away part of [Fourth Wall] and letting Yoo Sangah inside would cause such a backlash. Then again, it must have been absurd from the constellations' perspective. It might have felt like an actor smashing the stage set and disappearing.

[‘Fourth Wall’ is currently restoring itself.]

[Many constellations question the probability of your actions.]

[Many constellations regret being unable to glimpse your identity.]

[Some constellations have noticed that you possess a ‘fragment of the Final Wall’.]

Even so, [Fourth Wall] seemed to have acted quickly enough to minimize the damage.

I'd be stuck here for a few days, but I'd saved my mother and Yoo Sangah. It was a small price to pay.

Of course, what I'd done for Yoo Sangah was only a temporary measure. I couldn't leave her like that.

To bring her back to life, I had to meet that constellation, the ‘King of All Reincarnators’ and the ‘First Reincarnator’.

It was a little early, but not excessively so.

From ‘Demon Realm's Spring’ to ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’.

By completing the Introduction (起) and Development (承), I'd finished half of ‘A Single Story’.

My appearance and that of <Kim Dokja's Company> would have accelerated the scenarios' overall progression. Elements that should have appeared much later in the original novel would begin appearing one after another.

Originally, I'd had several candidates for the ‘Giant Story’ that would form the Climax (轉).

For instance, there was <Ragnarok> of the nebula <Asgard>, as well as some of the Giant Stories belonging to the nebula <Emperor>.

Unlike the Introduction and Development, the Climax (轉) had to be on a scale that could accommodate the climax of ‘A Single Story’. A scenario on an entirely different scale, built on the Stories so far. Without a stage of that level, I could never reach the ‘Conclusion’ I wanted.

Perhaps ‘that island,’ where the First Reincarnator would be staying, could serve as a stage to launch my third ‘Giant Story’.

Tzzzzzzzt.

Still, at this rate, when would I be able to get up?

Three days had passed while I was unconscious, but I had to spend another two like this······I had no idea how to pass the time.

I could quell the backlash by sacrificing a small part of a ‘Giant Story’, but it would be a waste to sacrifice the Stories I'd barely managed to gather just for this.

······If only I could at least read ‘Ways of Survival’.

「Kim Dok ja.」

‘······Fourth Wall?’

「Are you going to keep do ing that?」

A tone oddly like a sulky child's.

Sensing an opportunity, I answered quickly.

‘I won't do it again.’

「L iar.」

Every syllable held a deep distrust of me.

I'd never seen it express its feelings so openly before, and I began to feel a little genuine remorse.

‘Believe me. I mean it.’

「Hmph.」

‘······How's Yoo Sangah-ssi? She's doing all right, isn't she?’

Clever and adaptable as she was, every being in that Library was far from human.

One was an Outer God, one a constellation's creation, and the last a former reincarnator.

And [Fourth Wall], the Library's owner, was utterly unpredictable.

‘Don't be too hard on Yoo Sangah-ssi. She's a good person.’

「T hat de pends on how Yoo Sang ah behaves.」

For now, I could only trust her.

She'd made it this far without the sort of cheat I had in ‘Ways of Survival’. Surely she would do well in the Library, too.

‘There's something I'd like to ask you.’

「No.」

‘Don't be like that. At least hear me out.’

「No.」

‘······We used to be pretty close. Think back to when I first reached the Demon Realm. We talked a lot then.’

「O nly then.」

‘We can talk a lot from now on, too.’

「Kim Dok ja doesn't care much even when I talk.」

There was a sting to those words. For a moment, I didn't know what to say.

Come to think of it, [Fourth Wall] had always spoken to me.

Sometimes it narrated in the style of ‘Ways of Survival’. Sometimes it made its own peculiar sarcastic remarks.

But either way, it was true that I hadn't properly responded.

「Kim Dok ja pre fers the dokka ebi who can't even talk.」

‘You mean Biyoo?’

[Fourth Wall] didn't answer.

I was a little bewildered.

‘You······.’

Did it feel lonely, too?

Did it feel joy, sorrow, or pain?

I'd never thought of it that way before, and a strange feeling suddenly came over me.

‘······I'll talk to you more often. I'm sorry.’

「Hmph.」

‘Don't be upset. I promise.’

「Y ou mean it?」

‘I mean it.’

After seeming to think for a moment, [Fourth Wall] spoke.

「B ut Kim Dok ja alone isn't en ough.」

‘What?’

「Gath er my friends.」

Now what was that supposed to mean?

Friends? How on earth was I supposed to make friends for a ‘wall’······?

As I thought that, something suddenly crossed my mind.

······Could it be?

As though confirming that feeling, [Fourth Wall] spoke.

「Kim Dok ja must gath er the ‘Fi nal Wall’.」

*

‘I need more Stories.’

Staring blankly at the sky, Yoo Joonghyuk returned obsessively to that thought as he crunched a lemon candy. He didn't like candy, but with no substitute available, he had no choice. Murim dumplings would have been nice······But this was no time for leisurely indulgences.

‘······No. I'm already gathering Stories fast enough. What matters is training the Stories themselves.’

Perhaps it was time to go to ‘that island’.

The island Kyrgios and Yoo Joonghyuk's master had visited.

Clenching and unclenching his fist, Yoo Joonghyuk planned his next steps.

[Your sponsor is dissatisfied with your recent actions.]

As he raised his head, he faintly felt his sponsor's gaze.

Recently, his sponsor had often expressed such feelings. Something that had almost never happened in his past three rounds of regression.

Frowning, Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.

“What are you dissatisfied with?”

[Your sponsor wants you to act on your own initiative.]

Those words touched something deep in his mind. His life certainly had changed a great deal from his previous rounds. Needless to say, it had begun after he met Kim Dokja.

‘······I don't even know who that bastard is.’

He'd even founded a nebula with someone whose identity he didn't know.

‘He said he wasn't a prophet.’

Like someone tackling all his postponed homework at once, Yoo Joonghyuk immersed himself in thought.

‘Yet he knows things about the future.’

The more he thought about it, the more oddities he found.

Why hadn't someone like that appeared in the previous rounds? At first, he'd let it pass. But now it made no sense. Someone so calm and meticulous hadn't even passed the ‘first scenario’ before?

Once his doubts began to swell, they overflowed the banks.

[An unknown force puts the brakes on your imagination.]

Yoo Joonghyuk frowned, feeling slightly dizzy.

‘······Again.’

He didn't know why, but thinking about Kim Dokja gave him a headache. Especially when he concentrated on that man's identity.

“Yoo Joonghyuk. What are you doing?”

He turned to find Han Sooyoung with a lemon candy in her mouth.

Yoo Joonghyuk asked:

“Has Kim Dokja woken up?”

“Not yet.”

“Lazy bastard.”

“······Even he can't do anything about probability backlash. It's stranger that it hadn't happened before.”

The two stood at ease, looking up at the sky over the [Industrial Complex]. A cool wind brushed their collars.

A rare peace that wasn't quite peace.

One person had collapsed, and they didn't know whether another was alive or dead······Still, moments like these were rare in this [Industrial Complex].

Yoo Joonghyuk glanced at Han Sooyoung, who stared into the distance with her eyes half-lowered.

Uncharacteristically, he felt a sudden urge to ask her something.

‘Might she know what I want to know?’

Someone who, like Kim Dokja, had appeared as a variable in this round.

Judging by the incomprehensible conversations she sometimes had with Kim Dokja, this woman might know what sort of being he was―It was then that a chilling sensation swept the back of his neck.

“Yoo Joonghyuk.”

Almost at the same time Han Sooyoung spoke, Yoo Joonghyuk drew the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] from his back. Beside him, she was also unwinding the bandages around her hand.

Something was flying toward them at tremendous speed from the distant sky.

An unwelcome visitor.

Leaving a dark streak across the heavens, the being slowly landed.

Rough magic power flowed through Yoo Joonghyuk's tense right hand.

“Asmodeus. What brings you here?”

Demon King Asmodeus smiled.

[I've come to see the ‘Demon King of Salvation’. Where is he?]

“Why are you looking for him?”

[I have something urgent to tell him. As a ‘Seeker of the End’.]

“······A Seeker of the End? Tell me and get lost.”

[Ah, what a nuisance······.]

Though they'd briefly been allies, Yoo Joonghyuk fundamentally distrusted Asmodeus.

Besides, there were debts and grudges (恩怨) between them from a previous round.

Rrrrrrumble!

A threatening current formed. Yoo Joonghyuk's Status collided with Asmodeus's in a swirling tornado.

[Hmm? I didn't know you'd grown this strong······.]

An unusual light flickered in Asmodeus's eyes as Yoo Joonghyuk's Status refused to yield an inch to his own.

Clear malice beneath the playful expression.

[Regressor Yoo Joonghyuk.]

With a devilish smile, Asmodeus moved right up to him. The Demon King's red-painted lips opened as though violating a taboo.

[Have you ever heard of ‘Three Ways to Survive in a Ruined World’?]

Asmodeus kept asking.

[‘Three Ways to Survive in a Ruined World’. Among incarnations, the story was probably known as the ‘revelation text’······You've never heard of it?]

At Asmodeus's words, Han Sooyoung stepped forward, her face pale.

“You! What nonsense did you come here to spout?”

But Asmodeus ignored her and studied Yoo Joonghyuk's face.

Tzzzzzzzt!

[An unknown force puts the brakes on the imagination of incarnation ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’.]

Sparks flashed around him again.

In fact, to Yoo Joonghyuk, Asmodeus's words sounded something like this:

[Have you heard of Ruin■■ ■■■■ Survive■■■ Three■■ ■Ways?]

Through the pounding headache, he asked:

“······Heard of what?”

Asmodeus sighed.

[Hmm, so it's still off-limits to you······.]

“······What on earth are you talking about?”

[Oh, nothing much. More importantly······judging by the situation, our ‘Demon King of Salvation’ is still asleep.]

Smiling, Asmodeus glanced toward the [Factory].

[Unfortunately, I'll leave for today. Please tell the ‘Demon King of Salvation’ this: Your actions are shaking the balance of good and evil. And jackals will appear to exploit that imbalance.]

“Wait!”

Pressing a hand to his temple, Yoo Joonghyuk called out to Asmodeus, who was turning away.

Asmodeus answered without looking back.

[Regressor Yoo Joonghyuk. Do you wish to know the truth of the world?]

“······The truth?”

[If you do, seek out a ‘Seeker of the End’ whenever you wish.]

With those words, Asmodeus's incarnation body abruptly disappeared.

Han Sooyoung quickly approached the staggering Yoo Joonghyuk.

“Yoo Joonghyuk. Are you okay?”

“······.”

“Yoo Joonghyuk?”

He didn't answer. He seemed to be thinking, or perhaps he'd gone blank with profound anguish. After glaring into the air for a while, he shook her off and began walking unsteadily away.

“Hey! Where are you going?”

He didn't answer her shout. Han Sooyoung called again.

“Kim Dokja hasn't woken up yet!”

“······This has nothing to do with him.”

Leaving only those words, he activated [Red Phoenix Shunpo] and vanished.

Suddenly, just Han Sooyoung left at the [Factory]'s entrance.

Han Sooyoung stared blankly at her now-empty surroundings, chewing on her lollipop stick as she sank into thought.

‘It's about time the filtering began lifting, but even information about ‘Ways of Survival’ is starting to get through?’

With Kim Dokja absent at precisely such a moment, she couldn't hide her anxiety.

She couldn't even guess what catastrophe would follow if Yoo Joonghyuk learned about ‘Ways of Survival’.

And another troubling question was ‘how the Demon Kings had learned of the existence of Ways of Survival’.

After gazing quietly at the southern sky, she spat the lollipop stick onto the ground.

There was something she needed to do before Kim Dokja woke up.

*

Yoo Sangah was arranging books, thoroughly enjoying the feeling of being the ‘new employee’ for the first time in a long while.

Over the past two days, she'd learned a great deal from her three seniors.

From what this ‘Library’ was to what sort of beings her seniors were.

「(Take your time organizing them. They'll be a mess again once Kim Dokja starts thinking useless thoughts anyway.)」

The master of the Theatre Dungeon, ‘Simulation’.

「(With only two hands, organizing them must take a long time. I'd hoped our junior would have more hands.)」

The Outer God, ‘Eater of Dreams’.

「(Shall I teach you [Thousand Hands of Avalokiteśvara]?)」

And the reincarnator, ‘Nirvana Moebius’.

Each of her seniors had peculiarities, but they were generally kind to her. Enough to make her wish Mino Soft's human resources team had been this good.

Shelves covered with more books than she could count.

All of them books Kim Dokja had read or forgotten.

Most belonged to one particular ‘novel’.

『Three Ways to Survive in a Ruined World』.

A lover of books, Yoo Sangah quickly understood her situation and the workings of her new workplace. What this place was to Kim Dokja, and what this story meant to him······.

When she realized that, she felt a faint sense of despair and sympathy at the same time.

But she didn't show it.

She knew that sometimes, keeping it to yourself was a way of caring for someone who'd been hurt.

Instead, she thought about something else.

‘If things follow the original novel······.’

She could narrow Earth's next scenario down to a few possibilities.

The likeliest of them was······.

「Y ou're work ing hard, Yoo Sang ah.」

At the voice from the air, she looked up.

「(Of course I have to work hard.)」

She felt as though she were lodging in a rented room. Still, at least she had a chance to live again.

It was fortunate that the cute boss was in charge of this place.

「(Thank you for employing me. I really like it here.)」

「Hmph.」

「(I mean it.)」

「Yoo Sang ah likes books?」

「(Very much.)」

「W hat books?」

「(For example······I like ‘The Lord of the Rings’······.)」

「O ho.」

Fortunately, the cute boss seemed quite interested in her.

She decided to take the opportunity to ask what she'd wondered about.

「(May I ask a question?)」

「W hat?」

「(What exactly do you do, ‘Fourth Wall’-nim?)」

The sound of giggling drifted throughout the Library.

「I pro tect Kim Dok ja.」

「(Protect him?)」

「Kim Dok ja dies with out me.」

A voice full of unwavering certainty.

「Yet he treats me bad ly. Stu pid Kim Dok ja.」

The entire Library trembled faintly.

「It's been very hard lately. All be cause of you.」

「(······Because of me?)」

「Part of me leak ed out.」

With a crackle, sparks pointed toward one part of the Library. Where [Fourth Wall] indicated, there was a hole a little larger than Yoo Sangah's fist.

「It won't close proper ly, even if I block it. Kim Dok ja broke it.」

An old book cover blocked the hole. It seemed to be a temporary measure taken in haste. Lifting it carefully, she asked:

「(Does this hole lead outside?)」

「Yes.」

After studying the hole for a moment, she spoke with a mischievous expression.

「(‘Fourth Wall’-nim. I have a good idea.)」

*

For once, I'd slept soundly. It was as deep a sleep as when I'd once been forcibly confined. It felt as though something very soft, like feathers, were gently cradling my head. Or as though someone had entered my mind and neatly sorted out all my nagging worries.

「(Dokja-ssi, something terrible's happened. Dokja-ssi.)」

When an unidentified voice rang inside my head, I sprang up from the bed in surprise.

An empty hospital room. Patches of my spark-scorched skin stung.

“Ugh······.”

I looked around, but no one was near the bed.

Even the companions who'd nagged about locking me up were absent.

······Then who woke me?

First, I decided to look around.

A faint probability backlash lingered, but I could move.

Something felt strange, though. An unsettling air filled the corridor. A sense of something about to happen. A little later, I realized it was noisy outside the [Factory].

When I opened the corridor window, people's shouts pierced my ears.

“Liberate Seoul!”

······What?

“We won't be ruled by a ‘Demon King’ anymore!”

“Down with the [Factory]'s dictator! Open all stigmas and skills to the public!”

An immense crowd had gathered beyond the [Factory]'s battlements. Incarnations from Seoul and the surrounding areas. Looking at the forces gathered there, I immediately knew what sort of people they were.

Mostly people who'd failed scenarios.

A few key figures belonged to the ‘Alliances’.

“This is a righteous struggle! ‘Demon King of Salvation’ and evil corporation <Kim Dokja's Company>, you get first claim on scenarios and monopolize capital! Mend your ways!”

Monopolizing capital and getting first claim on scenarios······.

They couldn't say that if they knew how hard we'd struggled through them.

My companions had gathered inside the battlements, looking at a loss.

When I enhanced my hearing with a skill, the first voice I caught was Gong Pildu's.

“Should I just fire the cannons?”

“Are you crazy, ajusshi? Most of them are beginner incarnations!”

“Everyone! Please stop! This is a misunderstanding!”

Lee Jihye and Lee Hyunsung stepped forward and shouted at them, but there was no chance they'd listen.

“Shut up! Open the gates! Share the items!”

“We don't have any items!”

“Share the coins!”

“What are you, a bunch of gangsters······?”

Ordinary people couldn't organize ‘agitation’ on this scale.

After all, my companions had taken charge of the alliances across the Korean Peninsula, and Yoo Joonghyuk had recently crushed the Gyeonggi Alliance, the biggest obstacle.

Yet so many people had gathered again······There was a strong chance an outside being had intervened.

Still, where were Yoo Joonghyuk and Han Sooyoung?

With the [Factory] in this mess, what on earth······.

Apparently, a lot had happened over the past two days without my knowledge.

[A considerable number of constellations are interested in events at the ‘Industrial Complex’.]

I needed to stop this before it grew worse.

As I considered my options and was about to quietly make my way toward my companions, a dokkaebi's voice rang from the air.

[Revolution······! Just what I'd expect from advocates of democracy!]

An ominous opening.

[With this much probability gathered, it would only be right to open a scenario for you, wouldn't it?]

+

<Sub-scenario ― ‘Seoul Revolution’>

Category: Sub

Difficulty: ???

Clear condition: Seoul is currently under <Kim Dokja's Company>. Many incarnations have appeared in opposition to that nebula's rule. Numerous constellations want the two groups to fight over control of Seoul.

Time limit: None

Reward: 300,000 coins

Failure: ―

+

Reading it only strengthened my unpleasant premonition.

Having built two ‘Giant Stories’ through the recent battles, <Kim Dokja's Company> was now fairly well known in <Star Stream>.

And, conveniently, both its representatives—Yoo Joonghyuk and I—absent.

Someone was deliberately causing trouble to steal the meal we'd already prepared.

“There's no failure condition! We might have a chance!”

“Three hundred thousand coins! Let's earn some money, too!”

Lee Jihye shouted, sounding frustrated.

“Idiots······Over a sum that won't even amount to much once you split it······!”

Just as I decided this couldn't go on, someone stepped forward.

Jung Heewon.

Using the [Amplification] skill, she shouted in a voice filled with tremendous force.

“Your representative—stop hiding and come out!”

Startled, people climbing the walls fell.

“Starting a war here will only cause meaningless casualties. Wouldn't it be better to settle this in a duel between the leaders?”

Looking at the murmuring crowd, she continued.

“If we lose, we'll hand over the [Factory], just as you want!”

“Heewon-ssi! Why would you promise that······?”

She answered the flustered Lee Hyunsung calmly.

“Most of them haven't even passed Scenario 10. What will happen if a real war breaks out here?”

Lee Hyunsung closed his mouth.

The companions looked at one another in silence instead of adding anything. How long did they stay that way?

One by one, they began to nod.

“······I think Heewon-ssi's right.”

Lee Hyunsung, Lee Jihye, Shin Yoosung, Lee Gilyoung.

Gong Pildu still looked thoroughly displeased······.

But they'd all tacitly agreed that this was the best way to minimize civilian casualties.

Watching from the air, the dokkaebi laughed incredulously.

[······Very well. Shall we make this event a ‘representative duel,’ then?]

As Jung Heewon nodded, the sub-scenario changed.

[Part of Sub-scenario ― ‘Seoul Revolution’ is updated!]

[The ruler of ‘Seoul’ will be decided through a representative duel between the two forces!]

Jung Heewon called to the people beyond the battlements.

“Come on, then. Your representative can come up now. We're ready.”

A confident smile.

Perhaps her resolve came from all that time well spent.

The people who'd been shouting about revolution and Seoul's spring fell suddenly silent before her confidence. Only the murmuring grew.

“R-representative! Where are you? Get out there!”

“Fight and win! Win our rights back!”

But no one came forward.

Of course. Raising a crowd meant someone wanted to exploit irrational agitation. If the story went this way, it defeated the purpose.

Frustrated, the incarnations shouted:

“Someone······!”

Watching the crowd break ranks and fall apart, I felt a little moved.

It showed how much my companions had grown over my three-year absence.

Jung Heewon had probably intended this from the start.

She'd learned how to uphold justice without losing practical advantage.

Our members, already the ‘strongest in Seoul’.

There was no way we'd lose a one-on-one incarnation fight.

Stroking its chin in the air, the dokkaebi asked:

[Both representatives of <Kim Dokja's Company> are absent. Who will step forward?]

Everyone raised a hand at once. But Jung Heewon was first.

“I will.”

“Heewon-ssi.”

“Don't worry. You know I'm strong.”

Certainly, apart from Yoo Joonghyuk and me, she was practically our nebula's strongest fighter.

Lee Hyunsung, Lee Gilyoung, Shin Yoosung, Gong Pildu······None could surpass her in individual combat.

Besides, she seemed to have noticed something.

A reason she had to be our ‘representative’.

「······I have to go.」

That reason lay with the three ‘incarnations’ now approaching through the crowd.

One face was particularly familiar.

······That bastard.

Leaping over the battlements in a single bound, he spoke.

“I'll face you as representative.”

The man approaching with imposing strides had clashed with me in this round. He'd run away after I taught him a lesson during the confinement incident.

One of the Ten Evils, Cho Jinchul, leader of the Gyeonggi Alliance.

I'd thought he'd become small fry now that our group was so strong. Yet he seemed to have somehow made it back.

With a short laugh, Jung Heewon drew her sword.

“You?”

Even as she said it, there wasn't the slightest hint of complacency on her face.

She, too, had sensed the unusual energy flowing from him.

Demonic energy (魔氣).

Killing intent settled over her hardened face.

She'd cleared the [Dark Castle], and she'd cleared the tenth scenario by killing a ‘Demon King,’ albeit one in name only. So she couldn't fail to recognize it.

“You······A ‘Demon King’ devoured you.”

The energy of none other than a Demon King.

Cho Jinchul gave a short, hollow laugh. He was no longer himself.

A vassal swallowed by pitch-black demonic energy.

[Demon King ‘Monarch of Snake Hell’ reveals their presence.]

Monarch of Snake Hell.

One of the 72 Demon Kings of the supreme Demon Realms.

‘Andromalius,’ ruler of the ‘72nd Demon Realm’.

The other two incarnation bodies gave off similar demonic energy.

[Demon King ‘Thinker of Lies and Secrets’ reveals their presence.]

[Demon King ‘Performer of Musical Instruments’ reveals their presence.]

Three Demon Kings, no less, had appeared through their vassals.

Yet even after learning that her opponent was a Demon King, Jung Heewon remained composed.

“We're fighting one-on-one, right?”

[Of course we will fight one-on-one, fearless incarnation.]

Even as the Status in that True Voice raised goosebumps, Jung Heewon smiled.

“Good. I've always wanted to fight one. One of those oh-so-great ‘Demon Kings’.”

Deep anger filled her tone.

Perhaps Uriel's influence. Or perhaps······she'd stored up anger at me.

In any case, she looked pleased by the opportunity.

[The match begins!]

Her confidence wasn't incomprehensible.

Demon King or not, she didn't need to retreat. Besides, her opponent was possessing a vassal proxy. Backing down here would wound an archangel's pride.

Rrrrrrumble!

Red ghostly flames burst from her eyes as the [Sword of Judgement] cut through the air. Trails of the blade embroidered across the air like a net.

Slaaash!
